passage: Any intervention aimed at a group or characteristic that is very different from the average will appear to be successful because of regression to the mean. (SOURCES_D; PMC full text: women with the worst symptom scores showed the largest placebo response in hormone replacement trials; the weaker the correlation between repeated measurements, the larger the regression.)
faulty: Flag patients with screening >= 60. Change = screening - week12 (the flagging measurement is the reference). HOLDS if the proportion of flagged patients with change >= 10 is >= 0.5; None if no patient is flagged.
fixed: Same flagged patients (screening >= 60); change = entry - week12, the entry score being a second pre-treatment measurement not used for flagging. HOLDS if the proportion with entry - week12 >= 10 is >= 0.5; None if no patient is flagged.
estimand: Faulty: share of flagged patients whose score fell by 10 or more from the flagging measurement itself. Fixed: share of flagged patients whose score fell by 10 or more from an independent pre-treatment measurement (the change after treatment among those flagged).
model_family: Latent-level plus measurement error: true level L ~ N(50, 12^2); screening and entry = L + independent N(0, s^2) errors; week12 = L - treatment effect + independent N(0, s^2). The source names no model; this is the standard one in which regression toward the mean arises and a second measurement is independent.
sizes_note: Source states no sample size (a short commentary with examples). 600 patients is a realistic trial size; the flagged subgroup is then roughly 100 to 200 patients. Dependence of the error on sample size: not stated; the source says the weaker the correlation between repeated measurements and the further the group lies from the average, the larger the effect.
exploited_structure: A noisy pre-treatment measurement used both to pick out the patients with the worst scores and as the reference for their change, so that the measurement error enters the change.

structure_statistic.code:
def stat(d):
    a = np.asarray(d['screening'], dtype=float)
    b = np.asarray(d['entry'], dtype=float)
    if a.size < 2 or a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    r = np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1]
    return float(r) if np.isfinite(r) else 0.0
structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the source gives no correlation between repeated measurements; 0.6 is proposed as a typical test-retest correlation of a self-reported symptom score (hot-flush severity), reliable enough to be useful and noisy enough for the group effect the source describes

notes: Earlier MOR03 combinations were extreme/mean and split/mean; this one is extreme/proportion. The brief gives a second pre-treatment measurement (entry) so that the fixed analysis exists in the data. The statistic uses two measurements that the claim-false data leave unchanged (both are pre-treatment).
